01 / Execution

Make the authority to change explicit.

The existing portfolio describes BRAINK as a governed runtime: determine what may change, perform the transition and retain evidence that can be checked independently.

The customer problem

When automation crosses services, the difficult question is often who may act and what counts as success. A useful review makes the actor, requested change, target and recovery path explicit.

The architecture responsibility

BRAINK’s execution responsibility is distinct from IL‑LLM’s semantic responsibility and KEX’s structural responsibility. Interfaces must preserve that separation when a larger workflow combines them.

Relevant engineering

The deployment-queue source demonstrates evidence-bound lifecycle proposals and authenticated decision fixtures. Those are bounded engineering references, not proof that every BRAINK runtime is deployed or independently assessed.

Questions for an integration review

Which transitions are allowed? How are keys enrolled and revoked? What observable effects establish completion? Who can restore the previous state? These questions determine the interface and acceptance checks.

A considered next step

Describe a concrete transition and its present failure modes. An enquiry can help define a bounded evaluation; it does not initiate production changes.
